18   Funke to explain his vote.

19                SENATOR FUNKE:   Thank you, 

20   Mr. President.  

21                This bill helps deliver a measure of 

22   justice for one of my constituents.  His name is 

23   Ed O'Brien.  

24                Ed's son Kade was a Marine sergeant 

25   who served two tours in Iraq and was decorated 


                                                                2374

 1   for valor for fighting hand to hand and street to 

 2   street in Fallujah.  This brave Marine came home 

 3   a hero, settled down in Honeoye Falls in my 

 4   district, went back to school, had a son, and 

 5   pursued a law degree and a career in law 

 6   enforcement.

 7                On April 10, 2011, Kade was riding 

 8   his motorcycle in Mendon Ponds Park when he was 

 9   struck and critically injured by an inattentive 

10   driver who failed to properly yield the right of 

11   way.  He died the very next day.  

12                The driver whose actions led to 

13   Kade's death received only a $35 fine for failure 

14   to yield the right of way.  Thirty-five dollars 

15   for someone's life -- not fair, not right.  

16                Kade's father Ed came to me to work 

17   on a solution, but not out of a spirit of 

18   vengeance or anger.  He only wanted to raise 

19   awareness on this issue and educate drivers about 

20   it.  

21                This bill provides that anybody who 

22   kills or seriously injures another while failing 

23   to obey traffic law will be guilty of a 

24   misdemeanor with a penalty of up to 30 days in 

25   jail or a fine of at least $300.  And it requires 


                                                                2375

 1   any driver involved in one of these incidents to 

 2   complete a safety course to try to ensure that, 

 3   in this world of distracted driving today, they 

 4   pay attention so that we hopefully will never 

 5   make those kinds of mistakes again.  

 6                Ed O'Brien told me recently that 

 7   he's been diagnosed with cancer, and so he is 

 8   facing another tough fight ahead.  It's my hope 

 9   today that he will find some measure of comfort 

10   when we deliver this legislation in the name of 

11   his son, Sergeant Kade O'Brien.  

12                Mr. President, I vote aye.  I urge 

13   my colleagues to join me.  Thank you.

14                ACTING PRESIDENT CROCI:   Senator 

15   Funke to be recorded in the affirmative.

16                Senator Krueger.

17                SENATOR KRUEGER:   Thank you, 

18   Mr. President.  I rise to explain my vote no.

19                I appreciate very much Senator 

20   Funke's story with his constituent, and I am not 

21   opposed to his bill based on the fact that he is 

22   creating a model of $300 more or even up to 

23   30 days in jail.  

24                I actually don't think it goes far 

25   enough.  And actually, if it were to become law, 


                                                                2376

 1   it would have a lesser penalty or fine than law 

 2   we already have on the books, Section 1146 of the 

 3   rules of the road, which when a vehicle, if it 

 4   was to hit a pedestrian or a bicyclist, actually 

 5   could result in a higher misdemeanor charge and a 

 6   fine of up to $1,000, with the possibility of 

 7   police moving it into a negligence category.

 8                So my vote no is not a lack of 

 9   respect or concern for the story Senator Funke 

10   told, but rather that I actually think we have a 

11   stronger statute.  And that what Senator Funke 

12   might wish to do is to perhaps broaden the 

13   definitions within that statute to cover the 

14   situation as he just told that story, but not to 

15   end up with two sets of law in New York State for 

16   similar or even the same situation where existing 

17   law is actually stronger than this law would 

18   provide for.

19                And so that is my reason for voting 

20   no, Mr. President.  Thank you.

 1                I rise -- and Senator Krueger has 

 2   already explained the concerns that I have with

 5   Senator Funke that while I will be voting no, I

 9   others to make it stronger.  

10                Because I think we already have in 

11   law that which will cover the concerns that are 

12   raised in this bill, I will be voting no.

 3                I appreciate and respect the 

 4   sponsor's desire to address the issues of safety

10   broaden the definition of anyone and everyone 

11   within a facility having the right to all those

13                Two, it has an estimated cost 

14   annually of approximately $10 million, and 

15   therefore I feel that this should be dealt with

17   time.

18                And three, it actually, as I 

19   understand it, calls for a scenario that would 

20   have a one-to-one staffing ratio, one staff to 

21   one resident, within these facilities.  I don't 

22   really know any other parallel ratio in our 

23   criminal justice or our youth juvenile justice 

24   system, and I think that that is also a serious 

25   precedent that should be explored within the 


                                                                2382

 1   context of the budget of OCFS and its facilities.  

 2                And for all those reasons, I need to 

 3   vote no.

12                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this

23                THE SECRETARY:  "And WHEREAS, 

24   Attendant to such concern, and in full accord

                                                                2387

 1   Legislative Body is hereby justly proud to honor 

 2   Kayla McKeon upon the occasion of her designation 

 3   as recipient of the 2016 Champion of Change 

 4   Self-Advocate of the Year Award by the National 

 5   Down Syndrome Society, to be celebrated at an 

 6   award ceremony in Washington, D.C., on April 11, 

 7   2016; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, Kayla McKeon of Cicero, 

 9   New York, is a motivational speaker and community 

10   advocate with Down Syndrome whose positive  

11   attitude has inspired countless others to reach 

12   their highest potential; and 

13                "WHEREAS, As a motivational speaker, 

14   Kayla McKeon has delivered speeches at various 

15   venues, such as public schools and universities, 

16   throughout Central New York and the entire 

17   State of New York; in addition, she has conducted  

18   several media interviews to help raise community 

19   awareness about Down Syndrome; and 

20                "WHEREAS, Through her dedicated and 

21   enthusiastic advocacy, Kayla McKeon has proudly 

22   served as a strong voice for others with 

23   Down Syndrome; and 

24                "WHEREAS, In 2015, Kayla McKeon 

25   lobbied state legislators to help pass the 


                                                                2388

 1   New York Achieving a Better Life Experience 

 2   (NY ABLE) Act, which has since been signed into 

 3   law by Governor Andrew M. Cuomo; the NY ABLE Act 

 4   will allow people with disabilities and their 

 5   families to set up separate, tax-exempt savings 

 6   accounts to help them retain more of their own 

 7   money; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, Kayla McKeon met with 

 9   state lawmakers and used social media and 

10   speaking engagements to help gain increased 

11   support for the NY ABLE Act; and 

12                "WHEREAS, An accomplished athlete, 

13   Kayla McKeon has competed in a variety of Special 

14   Olympics events -- including floor hockey, track 

15   and field, and bocce -- since she was 13 years 

16   old on both the state and national level; and 

17                "WHEREAS, In June of 2011, Kayla 

18   McKeon became a World Games Athlete, proudly 

19   representing the United States and the State of 

20   New York in Athens, Greece, and ultimately 

21   brought home a Silver and Bronze Medal in bocce; 

22   and

24   Kayla McKeon is employed at Gigi's Playhouse in

 1   Congressman John Katko's office; this incredible
